key_insight: FREDI combines fair wireless resource allocation with dual-threshold early-exit inference to securely offload only critical events from edge devices to the server while preserving near-optimal utility and fairness.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical edge-AI control framework for latency-sensitive, security-aware deployments by jointly optimizing association, bandwidth, power, and confidence thresholds.
method: Proportional-fair optimization over UE–ES association, wireless/processing resources, and confidence thresholds
Dual-threshold early-exit CNN screening at each UE to flag critical events for secure edge offload
Exact threshold search on finite confidence values plus certified mixed-integer exponential-cone resource allocation
evidence_signal: Experiments with early-exit MobileNetV2 and ShuffleNetV2 show near-perfect UE fairness, utility close to a Sum-Utility benchmark, and Stage-A scalability from 6 to 144 UEs with median solve time below 0.1 s in tested cases.
watch_item: The approach relies on accurate empirical confidence distributions and exact/near-exact optimization assumptions, so performance may vary under nonstationary traffic, changing models, or real-time system constraints.
paper_title: Proportional-Fair Resource Allocation and Dual-Threshold Early-Exit Inference for Secure Cooperative Multi-Layer Edge Intelligence
